The benchmark presents a significant challenge to modern LLMs, with an average accuracy of 43.6% and 32.3% on some tasks. ## Overview

λ-GRPO is a method that addresses limitations in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), specifically improvements to Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).

## The Problem It Addresses

GRPO suffers from a length bias because the same advantage is uniformly assigned to all tokens of a response, causing longer responses to distribute the reward over more tokens and contribute disproportionately to gradient updates. Several variants like DAPO and Dr. GRPO modify token-level aggregation, but these methods remain heuristic with limited interpretability regarding their implicit token preferences.

## The Solution

The work explores allowing the model to learn its own token preference during optimization by introducing a learnable parameter λ that adaptively controls token-level weighting. When λ > 0, optimization favors longer responses; when λ < 0, it favors shorter ones, providing a flexible mechanism to balance different response lengths across tasks.

## Results

λ-GRPO achieves consistent improvements over vanilla GRPO and DAPO on multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks, improving average accuracy by +1.9%, +1.0%, and +1.7% on Qwen2.5 models with 1.5B, 3B, and 7B parameters respectively.
